correctness.rationale: The seven nonempty neighborhood types describe the entire finite space: sorting the n masks quotients pollinator permutations and does not quotient plant labels. For each survivor count k, each particular live set has probability p^k(1-p)^(n-k), and service is equivalent to an injective assignment of three plants to live pollinators. The independent replay used direct three-pollinator assignments rather than the frozen checker's Hall test. It exhausts (84,210,462,924,1716) mask multisets at orders 3–7 and verifies the connected/serviceable and missing-link filters; the complete graph is the unique missing-link exclusion at every order. For orders 3–6 each eligible graph has a candidate maximizing every gain coefficient. At seven, 1400 such certificates and 24 exceptions exhaust the 1424 eligible graphs. All exception gains are zero or have nonzero components (d3,d4)=(4,0),(5,0),(3,1); every exception has (3,1) and a pure d3 competitor. The stronger pure d3 competitor, if both exist, dominates the other, so the exhaustive vector classification reduces exact optimality to p^3(1-p)^3 times either 1-2p or 2-3p, with one strict interior sign change and a tie at its zero. Thus coefficient incomparability alone is not used as proof of a switch. The replay confirms the 9/15 split, all five plant-label orbits, and the first witness baseline (0,0,0,26,34,21,7,1), including the claimed B–0 and A–2 gain vectors, with all other candidates accounted for. This is a proof of the stated finite range, not a classification for n>7 or measured ecological behavior.

evidence: Perfect service here equivalently means a left-perfect matching after independently retaining right vertices. The adaptive catalogue match chooses the added link after observing survivors and starts from exclusive specialist classes. The quorum match permits shared pollinators and asks for two partners per plant.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Optimizing separately on each live set differs from choosing one action maximizing the probability over all live sets; a quorum condition without capacity is not a matching condition. Similar thresholds do not constitute equivalent statements.

originality.rationale: The strongest indexed matches considered include two distinct same-day records with similar threshold language. One changes the intervention timing and the graph design space; the other changes the service event. Neither covers the fixed initially connected incidence network and capacity-one, pre-failure addition classification. The exact indexed match is the frozen item itself. The primary comparisons cover different sampling, failure, or intervention questions. This is a best-of-knowledge finding, not an assertion of historical priority.
residual_risks: Statement-level comparisons are bounded; an unindexed fixed-graph vertex-reliability result for the same optimization could change the originality judgment. The unproductive outbound lookup is not negative evidence. Same-day dates give no independent priority inference.

value.rationale: The minimum size at which identical survival probabilities change the optimal pre-failure link is a meaningful property of the graph optimization: it tests whether the augmentation decision requires knowing p. The complete first-order exception classification and exact switches explain how saving more triples can lose to saving some quadruples. Choosing three service recipients and one new link is a motivated small matching reliability setting, and the result does not rely on a numerical grid or a claim of empirical pollination policy.
